hook.say: This morning, the post said Google launched one Gemini agent for business work, with identity, permissions, subagents, and auditability. I went back in to check what the product limits, pricing, and rollout details actually say.

findings.label: LIMITS
findings.headline: Business edition caps custom agent builds at 1 per day
findings.detail: The same plan also lists 120 text queries, 120 grounded searches, and 3 deep-research runs daily.
findings.evidence: Build agents (via No-Code Agent Building Tools) | 1 / day, pooled
findings.say: First, Google’s own quota page shows this is not unlimited. Business edition allows 1 custom agent build per day, pooled.

findings.label: PRICE
findings.headline: Entry price starts at $21 per seat per month
findings.detail: That is the public starting price on Google’s business page, before heavier platform usage pricing.
findings.evidence: Starting at $21 per seat per month
findings.say: Second, the entry point is priced like software, not magic. Google lists Gemini for business starting at 21 dollars per seat monthly.

findings.label: ROLLOUT
findings.headline: Google lists over 100 integrations, but key agent features are early access
findings.detail: Google says some capabilities shown, including delegated background tasks, are not yet available to all customers.
findings.say: Third, the connector story is broad with over 100 integrations, but Google also says some delegated background task features are still early access.

take.headline: Governance matters, but shipping still wins
take.say: My take: enterprise agents become real when identity, logs, and limits meet live workflows. Simple, governed automation beats a clever demo.

caption:
This morning’s post said Google is taking Gemini agents into business first, with governance as the real story.

1/day custom agent builds on Business edition.
$21 per seat per month is the public starting price.
100+ integrations are listed, but some delegated background features are still early access.

My take: shipping matters more than the demo. In production, limits, permissions, and audit trails decide whether the agent actually works.
